question.worked_solution:
The slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=\frac{e}{3}$ equals the function's derivative at the corresponding point.

We have the function 

$$
y=(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{{x}^{2}}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{{x}^{2}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & ={x}^{2}\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =({x}^{2})^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)))+({x}^{2})\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)))}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =2x\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))+{x}^{2}\cdot (\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)}\cdot \frac{1}{x}) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))+\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))+\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{{x}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{{x}^{2}}(2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))+\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of $y=(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{{x}^{2}}$ at $x=\frac{e}{3}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={y}^{′}{|}_{x=e/3} & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(e))^{(e/3)^{2}}(2(\frac{e}{3})\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(e))+\frac{(\frac{e}{3})}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)}) \\  & =(1)^{(e/3)^{2}}(2(\frac{e}{3})\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+\frac{(\frac{e}{3})}{1}) \\  & =1\cdot (0+\frac{e}{3}) \\  & =\frac{e}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
